papua-new-guinea.title: Flag of the Independent State of Papua New Guinea

colors.note: Traditional colour of the highland peoples
Traditional colour of the coastal peoples and the Southern Cross constellation
The Raggiana bird-of-paradise, the national bird
The stars of the Southern Cross

desc:
- Field divided diagonally from upper hoist to lower fly: red upper-fly with a yellow Raggiana bird-of-paradise, black lower-hoist with five white stars of the Southern Cross
- Adopted on 1 July 1971 and retained at independence on 16 September 1975

countryData.name: Papua New Guinea
countryData.officialName: Independent State of Papua New Guinea
countryData.location: eastern half of New Guinea and surrounding islands, Melanesia

trivia:
- Designed by 15-year-old Susan Karike, making it one of the few national flags created by a teenager
- Red and black were the traditional colours of many Papuan tribes long before unification
- The Raggiana bird-of-paradise in flight symbolises the nation's emergence into sovereign statehood
